title: Sum of Roman Councils: relative honorary adoration is owed—kiss, bow, incense—not latria; ask nothing from the image
source_text: XV. Ex quibus manifestum est, juxta doctrinam Ecclesiae Romanae, & Conciliorum illius placita, primo cultum aliquem, honorem & venerationem imaginibus Christi & sanctorum deberi. Secundo cultum illum legitime exhiberi imagines osculando, salutando & amplectendo, coram eis procumbendo, & caput aperiendo, ac ipsis offerendo suffitus & luminaria. Denique cultum illum adorationis voce recte exprimi. Non tamen imagines ut Deos adorandas esse, & cultu latriae colendas, id est, adoratione summa & absoluta, quae uni vero Deo reservanda est; sed adorationem quae illis exhiberi debet, subalternam esse sive relativam, & referri ad prototypa, atque in eis terminari. Adeoque ab imaginibus nihil esse petendum, nec ponendam esse in iis fiduciam, nec ullam divinitatem & virtutem iis tribui debere.
pass_a_gloss: From which it is manifest, according to the doctrine of the Roman Church and the decrees of her Councils, first that some cult, honor, and veneration are owed to the images of Christ and of the saints. Second that that cult is legitimately exhibited by kissing, saluting, and embracing the images, by prostrating before them and uncovering the head, and by offering them incense and lights. Finally that that cult is rightly expressed by the word adoration. Yet images are not to be adored as Gods and cultivated with the cult of latria, that is, with the supreme and absolute adoration which is to be reserved to the one true God; but the adoration which ought to be exhibited to them is subaltern or relative, and is referred to the prototypes and is terminated in them. And so nothing is to be sought from images, nor is trust to be placed in them, nor is any divinity and virtue to be attributed to them.
pass_b_english: Roman Councils agree: images are owed cult—kiss, salute, bow, incense, lights—and may be called ‘adoration.’
But only relative/subaltern adoration, ending in the prototype—not latria, not petitions, not trust or divinity in the image.

choices.english: to be terminated in them [the prototypes]
choices.why: Relative adoration’s terminus is the prototype, not the image-as-god.
